svg.text: Why almost all of the model can be skipped
the RAM is 4,096 memory heads (256 layers × 16). On every token, all of them check the address.
the one head that holds this address

g.text: A head that doesn't hold the address outputs exactly -0. The stepper proves that before doing the work:
1. Each head's 128 address rows are sums of ±256 per address bit. From this token's inputs it
bounds the largest of those sums: about 35 multiplies instead of 128 × 35.
2. If the bound, plus room for float rounding, is below -100, every row is below -100,
past the -89 where SiLU gives exactly -0: the head is skipped. A layer with no live head, whole.
3. So a skipped head gives the same output the full computation would: -0.
